{{short description|French statistician}}
{{use mdy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=April 2020}}
'''Dominique Marie-Annick Haughton''' is a French statistician whose research interests include [[business analytics]], [[Standard of living|standards of living]], and applications of statistics to [[music]]. She is a professor of mathematical sciences at [[Bentley University]].{{r|bentley}} She is also an associated researcher with the research center on Statistique, Analyse et Modélisation Multidisciplinaire at the [[University of Paris 1 Pantheon-Sorbonne]].{{r|cv}}

==Education and career==
After studying for the [[baccalauréat]] at the Lycée Pierre de la Ramée in [[Saint-Quentin, Aisne|Saint-Quentin]], in Northern France, and continued study at the [[Lycée privé Sainte-Geneviève]], Haughton entered the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|Ecole Normale Supérieure]] in Paris in 1975, where she earned a master's degree in mathematics in 1976, a [[Licentiate (degree)|licenciate]] in English in 1977, and a [[Diplôme d'études approfondies]] in mathematics in 1977. After a year at [[Harvard University]] as a Sachs scholar, she entered the Ph.D. program at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], and completed a Ph.D. in mathematics in 1983.{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, ''On the Choice of a Model to Fit Data from an Exponential Family'', was supervised by [[Richard M. Dudley]].{{r|mg}}

After working as an assistant professor at [[Swarthmore College]], [[Temple University]], and the [[University of Massachusetts Lowell|University of Lowell]], she joined the Bentley University faculty in 1991.{{r|cv}}

==Books==
Haughton is the co-author, with Mark-David McLaughlin, Kevin Mentzer, and Changan Zhang, of the book ''Movie Analytics: A Hollywood Introduction to Big Data'' (Springer, 2015).{{r|movie}} She is also the coauthor, with Jonathan Haughton, of ''Living Standards Analytics: Development through the Lens of Household Survey Data'' (Springer, 2011).{{r|lsa}}

==Recognition==
Haughton was named a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2011 "for outstanding collaborative research, outreach, and training in business analytics; for analysis of international living standards data; and for service to the profession".{{r|fasa}}
